bib.title: Evaluating Theory of Mind and Internal Beliefs in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Evaluating Theory of Mind and Internal Beliefs in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems", Adam Kostka and Jarosław A. Chudziak (Warsaw University of Technology). arXiv 2603.00142v1 [cs.MA], 24 Feb 2026. It is a preprint; the Springer-style layout and the Chist-Era grant note suggest a conference submission, but no venue is printed.

COVERAGE: 41,133 of 41,133 chars read, covering every page, the results table, the discussion, future work and the references. I did not run the figures script. Figure 5's data is a table in the extracted text, and the error-bar chart itself was not inspected.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- Claim: Adding ToM and internal beliefs (IB) with ASP verification does not reliably help. The authors conclude it depends on the model, the implementation and the task.
  number: none (qualitative)
  setup: 3 role agents (FOOD, MEDICAL, SECURITY) in a 4-district resource-allocation simulation. Metric is the median final district health. 5 LLMs, 4 configurations.
  quote: "the inclusion of ToM and IB mechanisms is not a universally performance-boosting feature for all LLMs."
  where: Conclusions, p.12

- Claim: For the strongest models the mechanisms add little or nothing. ChatGPT-4o stays within about 1 point of its base case in every configuration. Claude 3.5 Sonnet's gain appears only when ToM and IB are combined; ToM alone cut its score by 5 points.
  number: GPT-4o scores 69.44 (base), 68.89 (ToM only), 70.56 (IB only), 70.56 (both). Claude 3.5 Sonnet scores 68.89 (base), 63.89 (ToM only), 68.89 (IB only), 71.11 (both).
  setup: Median final health. I recomputed the configuration labels from the column order "With ToM (With IB, Without IB), Without ToM (With IB, Without IB)", so "base" is without ToM and without IB. No significance tests were run.
  quote: "ChatGPT-4o 70.56 68.89 70.56 69.44" and "Claude 3.5 Sonnet 71.11 63.89 68.89 68.89"
  where: Fig. 5 table, p.9

- Claim: Weaker models can be hurt by the machinery. For Llama 3.1 8B, IB alone and ToM+IB scored below the base case (35.00 to 26.34 and 30.02), while ToM alone helped (38.33). GPT-4o-mini was best with ToM only (59.00 vs 53.67 base), and IB alone or ToM+IB did not beat that.
  number: Llama 3.1 8B scores 35.00 (base), 38.33 (ToM only), 26.34 (IB only), 30.02 (both). GPT-4o-mini scores 53.67 (base), 59.00 (ToM only), 52.67 (IB only), 55.67 (both).
  setup: As above. The authors attribute the Llama drop to cognitive load, which is an explanation they did not test.
  quote: "Meta Llama 3.1 8B 30.02 38.33 26.34 35.00"
  where: p.9. Interpretation at pp.10-11: "the decline in the performance of Meta Llama 3.1 8B upon introducing IB to ToM also validate this, suggesting that the induced cognitive load is contrary at times."

- Claim: The weakest model, GPT-3.5-Turbo, gained the most from the full stack. It rose from 27.50 to 33.34, but stayed far below the strong models at about 70.
  number: 27.50 (base), 30.00 (ToM only), 27.50 (IB only), 33.34 (both).
  setup: As above.
  quote: "smaller models like ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo showed improvement in performance through the addition of ToM and IB."
  where: p.10; table p.9

- Claim: ToM predictions help capable models but cause miscoordination in weaker ones. The ASP check catches some logical errors, but natural-language vagueness limits it.
  number: none
  setup: Qualitative analysis of agent interactions. No counts are reported.
  quote: "Less capable models often made false predictions, leading to miscoordination, including ToM, which sometimes introduces cognitive load and compromises performance."
  where: §4.3, p.10

- Claim: Model choice matters far more than the added cognitive machinery. The spread across models (about 27 to 71) dwarfs the effect of any configuration.
  number: GPT-3.5 base 27.50, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 71.11 at best. Table above.
  setup: Same task.
  quote: "This shows that LLM choice and careful design of interaction mechanisms are highly significant factors in successful multi-agent cooperation."
  where: p.12

- Design detail: The ASP loop has up to 3 retries. It finds a minimal inconsistent subset by binary search over assumptions, then an LLM turns it into natural-language feedback. Consumption is 10 units per turn. Each trial has up to 7 turns per agent, which is 21 agent actions.
  quote: "This iterative process continues for up to three attempts."
  where: p.8

LIMITS
- The authors concede the task is simple: "the relatively simple nature of this task environment limits the generalizability of these findings."
- They say formal significance testing is missing and list it as future work: "formal statistical significance testing".
- The number of trials is never given ("multiple trials"). The only uncertainty shown is bootstrapped 95% CIs in Fig. 5, and the CI values are not in the text.
- There is no ablation of ASP verification apart from IB, since the IB-only configuration always includes ASP. The effect of the solver cannot be separated from the effect of the belief section.
- There are no cost, latency or token numbers, although the authors note that Clingo's cost is a constraint. There is no comparison to a single agent.
- Communication is sequential only. Only 3 agents and 4 districts were tested, and scalability was not tested.
- The models are dated: GPT-3.5-Turbo, 4o, 4o-mini, Llama 3.1 8B and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. No reasoning models were tested.
- Several differences are small, for example 4o at 68.89 vs 70.56 and Claude IB only at 68.89 vs base 68.89. Without significance tests they should not be read as effects.
- The cognitive-load explanations in the discussion are hypotheses, not measured.

BUILDS ON
- Li et al., EMNLP 2023 (ToM for multi-agent collaboration via LLMs).
- Jang et al., HAI 2023 (BDI structured prompting).
- Pan et al., Findings of EMNLP 2023 (Logic-LM, LLM plus symbolic solvers).
- Gelfond and Kahl 2014, and Gebser et al. 2013 (Answer Set Programming).
- Clingo as the solver.
- Kosinski, PNAS 2024 (ToM in LLMs).
- Xu et al., ACL 2024 (OpenToM).
- The authors' own earlier work: Kostka and Chudziak, PACLIC 2024.
- Related: MetaGPT (Hong et al., 2023), MegaAgent (Wang et al., 2024), Weng 2023 (agent blog post, source of Fig. 1).

CODE: none.

FIGURES
- Fig. 5, p.9: bootstrapped median final health with 95% CIs per model and configuration. It is the one figure worth reusing, because the sign of the effect flips by model. I did not inspect the chart image, only its data table.

PROBLEMS: The extraction was clean. No embedded instructions were found in the PDF. The Fig. 5 table's column headers are flattened, so I inferred the configuration labels from the header order. Check them against the chart before quoting configurations. The text is consistent with the order I used (Llama "best in ToM-only").
